hero.title: Interface physics for reliable memory and emerging electronics.
hero.description: Molecular contacts, defects, and ionic motion shape transport and state formation. I study these mechanisms in memory and optoelectronic devices, drawing on thin-film and flexible-electronics research while distinguishing current results from future integration goals.

map.ariaLabel: Research framework: molecular interfaces and defects inform memory state formation, optoelectronic memory, and reliability. Thin-film and flexible electronics are connected foundations. Integrated electronic systems are a future direction.
map.foundation: Connected foundations: organic & hybrid optoelectronics · flexible electronics R&D

vision.title: From interface-controlled transport to reliable, integrated memory
vision.intro: Published device studies establish how interfaces and defects affect transport and analog states. My ongoing work tests limits to memory precision and reliability; integrated memory hardware remains a longer-term research direction.
questions: How do molecular interfaces and defects govern electronic and ionic transport?
What limits the precision, stability, and reliability of emerging memory states?
How can device-level physics guide scalable memory and computing hardware?
